She has special needs, and now, years later, she told me that during her time there, certain things happened that affected her learning and mental health. She mentioned that safety was neglected at the madrassa: the stairs had gaps, knives were left out in the open in the kitchen, and the windows lacked screen nets. She also shared that the teachers would sometimes tell her and the other students to do chores when they were supposed to be completing their online schoolwork on PALCS. Furthermore, she brought up an incident where one of the teachers spilled bleach on her arm and instructed her to stay silent about it. She never told anyone, including her parents, until now. While I am unsure if all of this is completely true, seeing her current state makes me doubt she would make anything up. She currently experiences difficulty speaking and has severe hearing sensitivity. She has been receiving therapy, and the main reason I am writing this review is that her therapist reached out to inform me that many of her ongoing issues originated when she began attending this madrassa. Despite her past experiences there, I’ve noticed over the past few years that she has become very close to Islam. She remains deeply attached to her former classmates and makes dua for them daily. However, another issue she has faced for years is a deep worry for both the past and present students at the madrassa; to the point where she sometimes becomes physically ill from anxiety. She told me she attended the summer graduation on Sunday and was very relieved to hear an apology to the community, made after Dhuhr prayer by someone she assumed was Mufti Raihan. She believes the madrassa has changed, though it remains difficult to heal the harm caused during her time there. Thank you for reading. I wish the best for the present and future of this madrassa, and I pray that it continues to make up for the mistakes of the past. Ameen.
আমার এক কম বয়সী বান্ধবী ১১ বছর বয়সে এই মাদ্রাসায় পড়াশোনা করত। তার বিশেষ চাহিদা (special needs) রয়েছে; এখন, এত বছর পর সে আমাকে জানাল যে সেখানে থাকাকালীন এমন কিছু ঘটনা ঘটেছিল যা তার পড়াশোনা ও মানসিক স্বাস্থ্যের ওপর নেতিবাচক প্রভাব ফেলেছিল। সে উল্লেখ করেছে যে মাদ্রাসায় নিরাপত্তার বিষয়টি অবহেলা করা হতো: সিঁড়িতে ফাঁক ছিল, রান্নাঘরে ছুরি-কাঁচি খোলা অবস্থায় পড়ে থাকত এবং জানালার কোনো নিরাপত্তা-জাল (screen net) ছিল না। সে আরও জানিয়েছে যে, যখন তাদের PALCS-এর মাধ্যমে অনলাইন স্কুলের কাজ সম্পন্ন করার কথা ছিল, তখন শিক্ষকরা মাঝেমধ্যে তাকে ও অন্য শিক্ষার্থীদের দিয়ে ঘরের টুকিটাকি কাজ করাতেন। এছাড়া সে এমন একটি ঘটনার কথা বলেছে যেখানে একজন শিক্ষক তার হাতে ব্লিচ (bleach) ফেলে দিয়েছিলেন এবং তাকে বিষয়টি নিয়ে চুপ থাকতে বলেছিলেন। সে এতদিন পর্যন্ত তার বাবা-মা বা অন্য কাউকে এ কথা বলেনি। যদিও এসব ঘটনার সবটুকু পুরোপুরি সত্য কি না তা নিয়ে আমি নিশ্চিত নই, তবে তার বর্তমান অবস্থা দেখে মনে হয় না যে সে কোনো কিছু বানিয়ে বলছে। বর্তমানে কথা বলতে তার অসুবিধা হয় এবং শব্দের প্রতি তার তীব্র সংবেদনশীলতা (hearing sensitivity) রয়েছে। সে থেরাপি নিচ্ছে; আর এই রিভিউটি লেখার মূল কারণ হলো তার থেরাপিস্ট আমাকে জানিয়েছেন যে, তার বর্তমান অনেক সমস্যার সূত্রপাত হয়েছিল এই মাদ্রাসায় পড়ার সময় থেকেই। সেখানকার অতীতের অভিজ্ঞতা সত্ত্বেও, গত কয়েক বছরে আমি লক্ষ্য করেছি যে সে ইসলামের খুব কাছাকাছি চলে এসেছে। সে তার প্রাক্তন সহপাঠীদের সাথে গভীর সম্পর্ক বজায় রেখেছে এবং প্রতিদিন তাদের জন্য দোয়া করে। তবে, আরেকটি বিষয় যা তাকে বছরের পর বছর ধরে ভাবিয়ে তুলেছে তা হলো এই মাদ্রাসার অতীত ও বর্তমান শিক্ষার্থীদের নিয়ে গভীর দুশ্চিন্তা—এমনকি উদ্বেগের কারণে সে মাঝেমধ্যে শারীরিকভাবে অসুস্থও হয়ে পড়ে। সে আমাকে বলেছে যে গত রবিবার সে গ্রীষ্মকালীন গ্র্যাজুয়েশন অনুষ্ঠানে যোগ দিয়েছিল এবং জোহরের নামাজের পর মুফতি রায়হান বলে ধারণা করা এক ব্যক্তির কাছ থেকে সম্প্রদায়ের কাছে ক্ষমা চাওয়ার বিষয়টি শুনে সে বেশ স্বস্তি পেয়েছিল। সে বিশ্বাস করে যে মাদ্রাসাটির পরিবর্তন হয়েছে, যদিও সেখানে থাকাকালীন যে ক্ষতি হয়েছিল তা কাটিয়ে ওঠা কঠিন। পড়ার জন্য ধন্যবাদ। আমি এই মাদ্রাসার বর্তমান ও ভবিষ্যতের জন্য শুভকামনা জানাই এবং প্রার্থনা করি যেন এটি অতীতের ভুলগুলো শুধরে নেওয়ার প্রক্রিয়া অব্যাহত রাখে। আমিন।

I’m sharing this because this happened to my friend, and I really wish someone had explained the importance of mahr to her more clearly before her nikah.

One of the things that is supposed to protect the wife in an Islamic marriage is that the mahr is her right and something that belongs to her. In her case, the mahr was deferred as a promise of a future trip, leaving her without anything tangible or immediate that she could rely on.

I also know that many imams will not perform a nikah unless the mahr is clearly established and, in some cases, provided to the bride. I believe that kind of caution is important because the marriage should protect the woman as well, not just make it easier for the couple to get married.

Women should be encouraged to ask questions, understand their rights, and make sure their mahr provides real financial security before agreeing to a nikah.

reviews.name: Salomé
reviews.text:
Beautiful masjid, large, open, welcoming community. The events that are held keep the public in mind. That said, the teachings,  like most modern mosques, lean very much into Wahhabism—the “music is haram” kind of thing. They have the right to teach what they want, but some teachings take a conservative approach that does not keep victims and/or vulnerable people in mind. Hearing this as a brand-new revert is not exactly the most encouraging thing on the planet, amongst other teachings. There’s a bit of exclusion when it comes to what type of ideology is acceptable and what is not, but it’s subtle. They focus less on the mercy, compassion, and love Allah SWT has for the ummah, and more so on ways to improve and become a “better Muslim.” This could be helpful for a specific audience, but if you are dealing with complex mental health issues, domestic violence, or are looking for genuine support in your deen, you might want to find a more community- oriented or charity-based masjid. That said, the community that attends is home to some of the kindest, welcoming, and genuine people I’ve met. Just wish that same feeling was upheld whilst absorbing what is really being taught here.

They also don’t take domestic violence seriously at all in my personal experience. I had reached out for help getting out of my situation, which is unsafe; since I wasn’t “being hit”,  I don’t think they took it as a priority. I’m still waiting to hear back from them.

This place is good to attend if you are born-Muslim and Arab, or are a revert looking to immerse yourself into Arab Muslim or Wahhabi culture. Diversity is tolerated. The intellectual property of the people seems to be a bit stifled. Definitely room for improvement, but it’s a newer mosque. I hope for the team at Khair to see all as equal and deserving of support, insha’Allah. Alhamdulilah for this community.

—

Edit: I have reached out to this mosque about thirty times. I emailed the administrator for weeks, and they never got back to me.

I had asked for help finding resources for food, shelter, jobs, etc., because I was (and still am) living in an abusive environment. The imam said that he’d like to check in with me to see how I was doing on a regular basis. That still hasn’t happened.

I’m not sure if me being Black has anything to do with me not getting a response back. However, one of the (Arab!) sisters’ husband went on a long business trip a few months back, and the mosque set up a meal train for her and her children, alhamdulilah. I was left to fend for myself.

The imam interrogated me, asking me what I had done for myself to get myself out of this situation. When I told him everything I had done, he laughed and said something along the lines of, “Good. You know, if you weren’t doing anything to help yourself, I wouldn’t feel comfortable helping you.”

Wallahi, he told me to cook meals for my abuser to see if that helped our “relationship.” His prescription for abuse was more chores and housework and left it at that. Again, like I said, nobody at the mosque has gotten back to me yet. I met with them June of 2026. It is now October of that same year.

It’s possible Allah wanted to use this mosque to help bless a (newly reverted might I add!!) Muslim sister escape an abusive environment. Apparently, you only get help if you fit the mold that they require. I had been emailing them for months before I finally gave up. I’m not sure why they don’t seem to want to help everyone, but for whatever reason, I guess some people aren’t good enough to be helped. I’m not sure if I did something wrong along the way, but I’m not sure this is how the Sahaba would have acted. One of the sisters and her husband actually gifted me their zakat, which is honestly way more than the actual leaders of the mosque had ever done. While I am grateful, I am still in this awful situation, and I don’t know what I did wrong to not deserve help.

If you are Black, a new revert with lots of “unorthodox” questions, or queer, I would seriously reconsider attending this masjid. It’s a shame.
